notes.title: Reconstruction of the Complete Vocal Tract Contour Through Acoustic to Articulatory Inversion Using Real-Time MRI Data
notes.bp: Infer the shape of the whole vocal tract from the sound a speaker produces.
notes.wh: Speech acoustics are an indirect result of many moving articulators; EMA sees only selected points while MRI is broader but lower-resolution and temporally blurred.
notes.naive: Predict each contour point without accounting for articulator compensation or target-tracking error.
notes.ap: Train bidirectional LSTM models on denoised speech and real-time MRI contours, either articulator-by-articulator or all together.
notes.mech: The acoustic sequence is mapped to contour coordinates; phonetic segmentation is tested as an auxiliary signal and RMSE/median geometric error measure reconstruction.
notes.math: RMSE is average squared contour distance in millimetres; temporal sequence models use surrounding speech context.
notes.dots: Connects physical speech production to recognition and future articulatory simulation.
notes.ww: The paper reports 1.65 mm ABA and 1.69 mm AAT mean RMSE, compared with a 1.62 mm MRI pixel size.
notes.limits: The data are 2D MRI with 1.62 mm pixels and 8 mm slice thickness; acquisition and contour tracking introduce error. No independent reproduction was performed.

notes.title: Bridging ASR and LLMs for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Benchmarking Self-Supervised and Generative Approaches
notes.bp: Make transcription usable for dysarthric speech whose motor impairments distort phonemes, timing, and clarity.
notes.wh: Ordinary-speech recognizers fail when acoustic evidence is variable; CTC can misalign distorted phonemes and end-to-end systems can produce incoherent text.
notes.naive: Improve only the acoustic encoder and leave decoding without stronger linguistic constraints.
notes.ap: Benchmark Wav2Vec, HuBERT, and Whisper with CTC/sequence decoding and add BART, GPT-2, or Vicuna as language-aware decoders.
notes.mech: Acoustic representations produce candidates and an LLM uses context to select or repair sequences; WER is compared across TORGO and UASpeech.
notes.math: WER counts substitutions, deletions, and insertions; the key tradeoff is acoustic fidelity versus linguistic plausibility.
notes.dots: Bridges speech perception, language modeling, and accessibility rather than treating ASR as a generic benchmark.
notes.ww: The paper reports better Whisper results than CTC baselines and lower WER for LLM-assisted decoding in its experiments.
notes.limits: Cross-dataset generalization is poor, dysarthric data are limited, and not all encoder-decoder combinations were evaluated.

notes.title: Investigating the Reasoning Abilities of Large Language Models for Understanding Spoken Language in Interpersonal Interactions
notes.bp: Classify whether a job-interview answer is under-explained, succinct, comprehensive, or over-explained.
notes.wh: Spoken interaction requires judging an utterance relative to the question, prior context, and social task.
notes.naive: Use zero-shot prompting without examples, domain knowledge, or conversational context.
notes.ap: Compare few-shot examples, domain knowledge, and prior context across Gemini-1.5-pro, GPT-3.5-turbo, and GPT-4o.
notes.mech: Prompt factors condition a four-class decision; macro-F1 compares performance across classes.
notes.math: Macro-F1 averages per-class F1; context changes the evidence available for interpreting the same utterance.
notes.dots: Treats spoken-language understanding as social interpretation, not merely transcription or intent labels.
notes.ww: The paper reports selected macro-F1 results near 0.50 and 0.55 for its two tasks, with context and combined prompt factors sometimes helping.
notes.limits: The dataset focuses on military veterans and interview contexts; generalization across occupations, cultures, languages, and interaction styles is unresolved.

notes.title: Towards Better Disentanglement in Non-Autoregressive Zero-Shot Expressive Voice Conversion
notes.bp: Transfer a target speaker's voice and expression while preserving source linguistic content and reducing source-style leakage.
notes.wh: Speaker identity, words, emotion, pitch, and energy are mixed in speech, and parallel expressive data are scarce.
notes.naive: Use one style embedding, which can carry source timbre or content into the converted speech.
notes.ap: Combine multilingual discrete mHuBERT units, a conditional VAE, perturbation similarity loss, Mix-LN, pitch/energy features, and local-F0 cross-attention.
notes.mech: Content units encode linguistic material, style encoders represent speaker/emotion, and cross-attention injects local pitch into generated regions.
notes.math: Disentanglement allocates content and style to separable representations; cross-attention makes local target-pitch evidence influential where needed.
notes.dots: Connects generation to identity, expression, agency, and voice-conversion safety.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved emotion and speaker similarity and reduced source-style leakage versus its baselines.
notes.limits: The authors identify remaining intelligibility and cross-lingual challenges; this atlas did not run the model or inspect its demo independently.

notes.title: Location-Aware Target Speaker Extraction for Hearing Aids
notes.bp: Help a listener follow one person amid competing speakers, noise, and reverberation.
notes.wh: Microphones record mixtures and hearing aids impose strict latency and model-size limits; the target may move away from a fixed direction.
notes.naive: Use a fixed-direction separator or a one-hot direction code that cannot flexibly steer a small device.
notes.ap: Extend GCBFSnet with target direction of arrival, comparing one-hot and complex-exponential encodings and integration methods.
notes.mech: Binaural time-frequency features are conditioned on direction so learned filtering emphasizes the target; SI-SDR and intelligibility measures are evaluated.
notes.math: Complex exponentials encode direction through phase relationships; SI-SDR, HASPI, and MBSTOI represent signal and intelligibility outcomes.
notes.dots: Combines source separation, spatial acoustics, assistive technology, and on-device deployment.
notes.ww: The paper reports about +9.93 dB SI-SDR and +0.208 absolute HASPI for FILM-exp in its stated 1,000-utterance setup.
notes.limits: The evaluation is scenario-specific; future work includes direction estimation and scenes with more than two speakers. Objective scores are not clinical outcomes.

notes.title: VoxAging: Continuously Tracking Speaker Aging with a Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset in English and Mandarin
notes.bp: Measure how a voice changes over years and how that changes speaker-verification decisions.
notes.wh: Voice identity is not static; aging changes the vocal tract, while longitudinal data are difficult to collect.
notes.naive: Treat a speaker embedding or stored voiceprint as a permanent identity representation.
notes.ap: Introduce a longitudinal dataset of 293 speakers, weekly recordings, 7,522 hours, and a longest span of 17 years, then test verification over time.
notes.mech: Repeated observations allow verification scores and equal-error rates to be compared as the time gap grows, with age and gender analyses.
notes.math: Equal-error rate is where false-accept and false-reject rates meet; longitudinal evaluation makes identity time-dependent.
notes.dots: Connects representation learning to biometrics, dataset design, privacy, and the meaning of same speaker across a lifetime.
notes.ww: The paper reports declining verification performance and speaker similarity with increasing time span, with differences across age and gender groups.
notes.limits: The demographic and language composition is not universal; collection, labeling, and model execution were not independently audited here.

notes.title: Is it all about race? A Cross-examination of /s/ in a Multilingual Nigerian Context
notes.bp: Identify which social and linguistic factors shape /s/ pronunciation in Nigerian English.
notes.wh: Acoustic realization depends on neighboring segments, language ecology, age, ethnicity, and social context; imported categories can mislead.
notes.naive: Explain /s/ variation mainly through gender or race based on studies from other linguistic settings.
notes.ap: Analyze 4,056 /s/ tokens from ICE-NigE using center of gravity, zero crossings, duration, and skewness across ethnicity, age, gender, and phonological context.
notes.mech: Acoustic measurements operationalize frontness/backness and duration; statistical comparisons associate variation with linguistic and sociolinguistic factors.
notes.math: Spectral center of gravity, zero crossings, and skewness summarize signal distribution as proxies for articulation and social patterning.
notes.dots: Shows why accents and social variation should be modeled as meaningful local structure rather than generic nuisance variation.
notes.ww: The paper reports age and ethnicity effects among Igbo, Yoruba, and Hausa Nigerian English speakers, with limited gender differences in this analysis.
notes.limits: The result concerns this corpus and phoneme; acoustic measures should not be treated as direct proof of identity categories.

notes.title: Enabling the replicability of speech synthesis perceptual evaluations
notes.bp: Make subjective speech-synthesis evaluations sufficiently specified for meaningful repetition and comparison.
notes.wh: Listener ratings depend on questions, framing, participants, stimuli, and protocol, while headline MOS-style scores hide those choices.
notes.naive: Report a perceptual score without the question asked or the evaluation recipe.
notes.ap: Propose a standardized report, shareable evaluation recipe, open-source platform, and reporting guidelines.
notes.mech: Separate the readable report from supplementary procedural data; distinguish reproducibility with the same inputs from replicability across new participants and data.
notes.math: A subjective score is an observation produced by a protocol, not a property of a waveform independent of listeners; omitted protocol variables become unmeasured variance.
notes.dots: Provides a methodological backbone for judging speech claims throughout the atlas.
notes.ww: The contribution is a proposed platform and reporting structure intended to make evaluation choices inspectable.
notes.limits: Human subjective evaluations cannot simply be rerun with identical participants; adoption and future standards remain open, and the platform was not executed here.
